key_insight: LLM-based radiology metrics can detect clinically important errors, but many also overreact to harmless wording changes, so the key challenge is balancing discrimination with robustness.
clinical_relevance: A better metric for report evaluation could more reliably flag dangerous omissions or misstatements while avoiding unnecessary penalties for acceptable rephrasings.
method: Benchmarked 8 LLM evaluators on the ReEvalMed testbed.
Measured two metric behaviors: discrimination of true clinical errors and robustness to harmless variation.
Trained lightweight interpretable metrics on 4k synthetic report pairs using Qwen3-8B and MedGemma-4B.
evidence_signal: Across one-pass and two-pass settings, the study found a common discrimination bias; the trained metric outperformed 32B-scale medical LLMs and was competitive with proprietary models.
watch_item: The two-pass setup was not consistently better and can trade robustness for error detection, so deployment choices should be validated for the intended clinical evaluation goal.
paper_title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
